title: Using GeoAI and machine learning tools for consistent high-resolution land cover mapping based on time-series NAIP imagery
relevance: Closest published analogue to our problem: temporally consistent high-resolution land cover from a NAIP time series, and it reports that NAIP imagery acquired in the SAME year still shows pronounced domain discrepancies across regions. That is a stronger statement than our consensus finding (a) - if within-year, within-sensor drift is already material, our cross-contractor King 2000 vs King 2019 gap is not an outlier and cannot be assumed away. Gives a published workflow for enforcing temporal consistency that we should compare against our anchor-and-project design.

authors: Luo, M., Zan, Y., Khoshelham, K. & Ji, S.
title: Domain generalization for semantic segmentation of remote sensing images via vision foundation model fine-tuning
source: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 230, 126-146
relevance: Peer-reviewed treatment of the exact failure our consensus finding (a) names - augmentation bridges resolution but not sensor/radiometry - and shows that fine-tuning a vision foundation model generalizes across unseen domains far better than training from scratch or augmenting. Directly relevant to whether our single shared ResNet-101 U-Net backbone is the right base, or whether a VFM encoder would absorb the sensor/era shift we currently try to fix with normalization. This is a concrete, testable alternative to the radiometric-normalization workstream (open item 3), not a complement to it.

title: Investigating class granularity in historical aerial image segmentation: a comparative analysis of CNN and transformer-based models
relevance: Benchmarks CNNs (DeepLabV3+, PSPNet, HRNet, ConvNeXt) against transformers (ViT, Swin, BEiT) specifically on HISTORICAL aerial imagery, and varies class granularity - how finely the legend is cut - as the independent variable. Two things we need: whether architecture choice matters more on historical imagery than it does on modern (our finding 2 says model strength does not move the number, but that was measured only on modern-era years), and evidence on how much our canopy-vs-shrub granularity decision costs us. Directly tests a claim we have only verified post-2013.

title: Reconstructing a century of urban growth through deep learning-based colorization and segmentation of historical aerial and satellite imagery: Les Sables-d'Olonne, France (1920-2024)
relevance: Bridges a century-scale domain gap by colorizing panchromatic historical aerial photography (attention-enhanced Pix2Pix) then segmenting with a few-shot U-Net++, on a 1920-2024 series - structurally the same shape as our 2000-2024 problem with a harder input. Offers a route for our King 2000/2002 HARD FLOOR that we have not considered: synthesize the missing radiometry rather than normalize toward it. Treat the reported gains cautiously - colorization invents plausible colour, which is exactly the kind of hallucinated evidence our honest-measurement rule exists to exclude, so any adoption needs an in-year Olofsson check.

title: D2FT-Net: Frequency-spatial dual domain fine-tuning of vision foundation models for remote sensing domain generalization semantic segmentation
source: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing 64, 5621016
relevance: Fine-tunes a vision foundation model in the FREQUENCY domain as well as the spatial one for domain-generalized segmentation. Relevant because sensor and contractor differences show up largely as texture/sharpening/compression signatures - frequency-domain artifacts - which is plausibly why our spatial augmentation spans 8x GSD but not the King contractor change. Suggests a cheap diagnostic before any retrain: compare per-year power spectra across our 18 acquisitions to see whether the eras separate in frequency space.

title: CrossEarth: Geospatial vision foundation model for domain generalizable remote sensing semantic segmentation
relevance: First vision foundation model built specifically for remote-sensing domain generalization, benchmarked over 32 cross-domain settings spanning location, wavelength, sensor, platform and climate - the same axes we span across King/Snohomish/NAIP. Its Earth-Style Injection pipeline is a generative alternative to radiometric normalization that operates on style rather than on histograms. Flagged PREPRINT: use as a design reference and a source of benchmark structure, not as evidence, until it has a venue.
